paper_metadata.title: A comparison study on microstructures and fracture behaviours of a single NbSS solid solution alloy and a two-phase NbSS/Nb5Si3 alloy prepared by spark plasma sintering and arc melting

Button ingot with a weight of 2500 g was prepared by vacuum arc melting (AM) six times to obtain homogenization composition throughout the ingot.

For each alloy, three ingots were fabricated, and they were then re-melted together in a vacuum induction (VIM) furnace and cast into a columnar graphite mould to produce an electrode bar with size of 75 mm in diameter and 150 mm in length.
The power of the plasma gun was 200 kW and the speed of the rotating electrode (the VIM single NbSS phase alloy and two-phase NbSS/Nb5Si3 alloy bars) was 10 – 15 thousands rpm.

The PREA single NbSS phase alloy and two-phase NbSS/Nb5Si3 alloy powders with a weight of 60 g were placed into a BN-coated graphite die with dimensions of Φ 30 × 60 mm and then sintered at 1350 ◦C for 5 min under 50 MPa in an argon atmosphere using a spark plasma sintering system (SPS-1050), followed by furnace cooling.

The SPS sample has a uniform and dense microstructure (with a relative density (ρ) larger than 99.36% (Fig. 3a)) without visible defects, and its microstructure consists of a continuous NbSS matrix and equiaxed- and worm-like Nb5Si3 islands, as can be seen in Fig. 3a’.
The Nb5Si3 islands are 1 – 2 μm in size and the NbSS phase between the Nb5Si3 islands has a width at the same level as that of the Nb5Si3 islands.
the primary NbSS strip has dimension of approximately 50 – 80 μm in length and ~ 20 μm in width
